newsitem.title: GERMANY: DTB to offer more products to U.S.-based traders.
newsitem.headline: DTB to offer more products to U.S.-based traders.

text.p: Germany futures and options exchange, Deutsche Terminboerse is increasing the number of products made available to traders based in the United States, the German bourse group Deutsche Boerse said.

In a statement, the German bourse said U.S.-based traders, who are already allowed to trade some DTB products, would also be allowed to trade one-month Euromark futures, which were introduced on November 12.
Three-month Euromark futures and also dollar/mark options would also be able to be traded from the U.S. once they had been introduced in January, the bourse said.
DTB to offer more products to U.S.-based =2

Currently U.S.-based traders can trade futures on German 10-year government bonds or Bunds and five-year issues BOBLs, as well as the options on these two products and futures on the 30-share DAX index.
Deutsche Boerse board member Joerg Franke said in the statement that the new arrangements gave the DTB a considerable competitive advantage.
"We are the first bourse which can offer the full interest rate curve in a European currency directly to U.S. investors," he said.

The news comes one day after the Chicago Mercantile Exchange announced that it plans to begin trading French bond contracts from the French exchange MATIF and short-term interest rate contracts listed on London's LIFFE.
